title: Invocation ancestry graph and compact path IDs for Console analytics
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: current Console usage tables surface per-invocation rows but lack a compact, stable identifier for an invocation 'path' (the ordered sequence of internal steps: route -> model_variant -> tool calls -> post-processing). This makes it expensive to deduplicate recurring invocation sequences, attribute cost/latency to a canonical path, or compute ancestry (which invocation preceded/caused another) for debugging and SLO analysis.

Goals:
- Introduce a curated invocation_paths table that stores a canonical representation of observed invocation sequences and a compact path_id that can be used as a stable key in downstream rollups.
- Provide an ancestry graph representation (parent_path_id links) for quick traversal of common prefix/suffix relationships and for impact analysis when model variants change.
- Enable fast rollups by tenant and route that attribute cost and latency to path_id rather than raw per-event sequences, reducing join cardinality for analytics dashboards and alerting.
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing route/tenant-level metrics and provide an incremental backfill strategy.

Scope: schema design, ingestion SQL/ETL, compact ID function, batching strategy, rollup tables, QA, and migration runbook.
acceptance_criteria: curated.invocation_paths table created with stable path_id and canonical path text for >95% of daily invocations
path_id is <=64 bits when represented as hex string and collision rate measured <1e-12 for simulated corpus
daily tenant_path_rollups table uses path_id as primary grouping key and reduces join cost by >=40% in typical console dashboards
ancestry graph accessible via curated.invocation_path_graph with parent_path_id links for top 100k paths
migration script and backfill runbook documented and tested in staging cluster
QA: sample queries against console-2025.03 dashboards show identical aggregate totals (count/cost/latency p50/p95) within 0.1% after rollup alignment
design_decisions: Compact ID format: use BigQuery FARM_FINGERPRINT on canonical_path_text then hex-encode 64-bit value; store as STRING 'pf_<hex>' to reserve namespace for future versions

Canonical path representation: ordered JSON array of minimal step tokens (route_id, model_variant, tool:set, step_flags) with deterministic normalization rules (lowercase, stable variant alias mapping, strip ephemeral tokens)

Ancestry graph model: store immediate parent_path_id computed by truncating the last step from canonical path; allow multiple parents when different sequences converge to same suffix; materialize top-k parents per path to bound graph size
Precompute vs on-demand: precompute daily canonicalization and path_id assignment to optimize dashboard joins; retain raw events for on-demand recompute if canonicalization rules change

Partitioning & clustering: invocation_paths partitioned by first_seen_date (DATE) and clustered by path_length, tenant_id to optimize common queries; rollups partitioned by usage_date and clustered by path_id, tenant_id
Retention: keep curated.invocation_paths for 365 days with option to archive to cheaper storage for older footprints
implementation_plan: Step 1: Add normalization library to ingestion Helm job (python module) that builds canonical_path_text from raw callstream
Step 2: Create staging table analytics_staging.canonical_paths_raw (daily append) and implement dedup window to reduce churn
Step 3: Batch job (airflow) to compute path_id using FARM_FINGERPRINT and write to curated.invocation_paths with first_seen_date and representative metrics
Step 4: Build curated.invocation_path_graph by computing parent_path_id via SQL string manipulation on canonical_path_text and materialize top-parents
Step 5: Modify tenant_path_rollups_ETL to group on path_id instead of full path text and add fallbacks for unknown path_id values
Step 6: Backfill strategy for last 90 days in two phases: large window fast-path (sampling + incremental) then full backfill throttled by slot quotas
Step 7: Instrument dashboards (console) to display path_id and small human-readable canonical snippet for top N paths
Step 8: QA, load tests, and staged rollout with canaries in dev and staging followed by prod rollforward
migration_plan: Run local canonicalizer over a 7-day sample and validate path_id collision rate against simulated inputs
Deploy canonicalizer and staging tables to staging cluster and run full 30-day backfill; compare aggregates to existing rollups
Execute incremental production backfill for 14 days with consumer dashboards in read-only mode and validation checks enabled
Flip ETL: switch rollup job to read path_id field; keep compatibility column legacy_path_text for 30 days; monitor drift and metrics
Finalize: drop legacy_path_text after 30 days and trigger archival of old invocation_paths beyond retention window
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): enable canonicalizer for 5% of incoming traffic for non-critical tenants; compare compute and storage metrics
Week 2 (staged): run daily batch on full staging data; perform end-to-end validation against console dashboards
Week 3 (prod): enable for all tenants but keep legacy_path_text persisted; monitor collisions, rollup variance, API latency
Rollback strategy: if collision rate or rollup delta exceeds thresholds, revert rollup job to group by legacy_path_text and pause canonicalizer
Post-mortem window: 7 days of intensified monitoring and weekly stake-holder syncs until two consecutive weeks of stable metrics
metrics: Collision rate (simulated and observed) per 1e9 hashed paths
Join time reduction in dashboard queries (ms) and query slot consumption
Storage delta: size of curated.invocation_paths vs raw path text column
Aggregate parity: difference in count/cost/latency compared to legacy rollups
SLO impact: percent of alerts that can be traced to a path_id within 5 minutes
sample_sql:
-- BigQuery example: compute compact path id and write to curated table
INSERT INTO curated.invocation_paths (path_id, canonical_path_text, tenant_id, path_length, first_seen_date)
SELECT
  CONCAT('pf_', TO_HEX(FARM_FINGERPRINT(canonical_path_text))) AS path_id,
  canonical_path_text,
  tenant_id,
  ARRAY_LENGTH(split(canonical_path_text,'|')) AS path_length,
  DATE(event_timestamp) AS first_seen_date
FROM analytics_staging.canonical_paths_raw
WHERE DATE(event_timestamp) = @process_date;
comments: 2025-03-02 - Ava Chen: Kickoff sync with PM & data platform. Agreed canonicalization must strip ephemeral tokens and map variant aliases from model_onboard_service. Action: Liam to prototype normalizer.

2025-03-04 - Liam Ortega: Prototype normalizer complete. Edge cases: tool call ordering varies; decided to sort deterministic tool sub-steps by stable key when they are commutative (eg. parallel tools).
2025-03-06 - Design review: noted potential collision vector when canonical_path_text grows long; decision to use FARM_FINGERPRINT + namespace prefix and record path_length for extra safety.

2025-03-08 - Data infra: slot usage estimate for full 90-day backfill is ~4500 slot-hours; agreed to chunk and throttle to avoid quota exhaustion. See GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1267

2025-03-10 - QA: initial staging run produced 1.2M unique path_ids for 7-day sample; top 5k paths cover 78% of calls which validates rollup approach. Dashboard query speed improved ~52% in staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/342

2025-03-12 - Lina Raghavan (PM): Approved migration plan pending one change — include runbook step to notify customers with long-running custom analytics that reference legacy_path_text. Action: add notification step to runbook.
